scanner: OWASP ZAP v2.17.0 (Passive Proxy Mode during Playwright Workflows A & B)

findings.solution:
Ensure that sensitive data is not available in an unauthenticated manner (using IP address white-listing, for instance).
Configure the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" HTTP header to a more restrictive set of domains, or remove all CORS headers entirely, to allow the web browser to enforce the Same Origin Policy (SOP) in a more restrictive manner.
This is an informational alert rather than a vulnerability and so there is nothing to fix.

Ensure that the application/web server sets the Content-Type header appropriately, and that it sets the X-Content-Type-Options header to 'nosniff' for all web pages.
If possible, ensure that the end user uses a standards-compliant and modern web browser that does not perform MIME-sniffing at all, or that can be directed by the web application/web server to not perform MIME-sniffing.

findings.alert: CSP: Failure to Define Directive with No Fallback
findings.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is properly configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.
Ensure that the HttpOnly flag is set for all cookies.
Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to either 'lax' or ideally 'strict' for all cookies.

Phase: Architecture and Design
Use a vetted library or framework that does not allow this weakness to occur or provides constructs that make this weakness easier to avoid.
For example, use anti-CSRF packages such as the OWASP CSRFGuard.

Phase: Implementation
Ensure that your application is free of cross-site scripting issues, because most CSRF defenses can be bypassed using attacker-controlled script.

Phase: Architecture and Design
Generate a unique nonce for each form, place the nonce into the form, and verify the nonce upon receipt of the form. Be sure that the nonce is not predictable (CWE-330).
Note that this can be bypassed using XSS.

Identify especially dangerous operations. When the user performs a dangerous operation, send a separate confirmation request to ensure that the user intended to perform that operation.
Note that this can be bypassed using XSS.

Use the ESAPI Session Management control.
This control includes a component for CSRF.

Do not use the GET method for any request that triggers a state change.

Phase: Implementation
Check the HTTP Referer header to see if the request originated from an expected page. This could break legitimate functionality, because users or proxies may have disabled sending the Referer for privacy reasons.
This is an informational alert and so no changes are required.
Manually confirm that the timestamp data is not sensitive, and that the data cannot be aggregated to disclose exploitable patterns.
Upgrade to the latest version of the affected library.

findings.alert: User Controllable HTML Element Attribute (Potential XSS)
findings.solution: Validate all input and sanitize output it before writing to any HTML attributes.
Remove all comments that return information that may help an attacker and fix any underlying problems they refer to.

Modern Web browsers support the Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options HTTP headers. Ensure one of them is set on all web pages returned by your site/app.
If you expect the page to be framed only by pages on your server (e.g. it's part of a FRAMESET) then you'll want to use SAMEORIGIN, otherwise if you never expect the page to be framed, you should use DENY. Alternatively consider implementing Content Security Policy's "frame-ancestors" directive.

findings.alert: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
findings.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.
This is an informational alert rather than a vulnerability and so there is nothing to fix.

configuration_evidence.observed_state: HttpOnly attribute verified on pretix_session across authenticated Playwright sessions
configuration_evidence.config_corroboration: pretix/settings.py: SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = True (prevents JS access to session identifiers)

configuration_evidence.observed_state: SameSite=Lax verified on cookies; state-mutating POST rejected with 403 Forbidden without CSRF token
X-Frame-Options: DENY observed across storefront and control panel routes
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff observed on HTTP responses
configuration_evidence.config_corroboration: pretix/settings.py: SECURE_CONTENT_TYPE_NOSNIFF = True, enforced by SecurityMiddleware
